newsitem.title: MONACO: Monaco seeks French help to introduce euro.
newsitem.headline: Monaco seeks French help to introduce euro.

text.p: Prince Rainier of Monaco asked visiting French President Jacques Chirac on Friday for help in introducing the European Union's planned single currency in the tiny principality in tandem with France.

"The principality wants the French government to help it, in accordance with the spirit of our treaties, to find its place in a (new) Europe and to give legal currency to the euro at the same date as in France," Rainier said.

The French franc is the legal currency in the Riviera state, which has a population of just 30,000 squeezed into less than two sq km (one sq mile) by the Mediterranean. France wants to join the single currency, the euro, which is due to be launched in January1999.
Rainier said that his principality, celebrating its 700th anniversary, was "very open to any joint discussion about its possible role beside France in the world of tomorrow".

Chirac, making only the third official visit by a French president to Monaco since the start of France's Fifth Republic in 1958, met Rainier for about 40 minutes in his palace overlooking the Mediterranean.
"Monaco is a full partner in the European Union which, day after day, is growing stronger, deeper and larger," Chirac said.
"Already, and it's a strong symbol of your association with Europe, we have begun discussions about the introduction of the euro in the principality," Chirac said.
He said that the two countries had a "perfect understanding".
Chirac was accompanied by French Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine for a visit of several hours. Rainier's Grimaldi dynasty is celebrating its 700th year in power.
